test-no-arch.name: Test Project
test-no-arch.idea: A smart parking system to detect available parking slots

smart-helmet.name: Smart Helmet Safety System
smart-helmet.idea: A connected motorcycle helmet that enforces safety compliance by preventing ignition unless the helmet is worn and chin strap is fastened, with real-time wireless communication to the bike.
smart-helmet.objective: Prevent motorcycle accidents caused by improper helmet use by creating an automated safety interlock system with real-time feedback.
smart-helmet.constraints: Must operate within motorcycle helmet constraints - very limited space, battery powered with minimum 6 month standby, must survive vibration and weather exposure, cost under $15 per unit.

test-no-arch.problem: Drivers waste time and fuel searching for available parking spaces in urban areas. A low-cost, IoT-based smart parking system using ESP32 microcontrollers and MQTT communication is needed to detect slot occupancy in real-time and guide drivers to open spots quickly.

functional_requirements.title: Parking Slot Occupancy Detection
functional_requirements.description: Each parking slot shall be monitored by an ESP32-based sensor node capable of detecting vehicle presence (e.g., ultrasonic, IR, or magnetic sensor) and reporting status changes in real-time.

functional_requirements.title: Real-Time Status Publishing via MQTT
functional_requirements.description: Sensor nodes shall publish slot occupancy status (occupied/free) to an MQTT broker immediately upon state change, with periodic heartbeat messages every 30 seconds to confirm node liveness.

functional_requirements.title: Centralized Parking Map Aggregation
functional_requirements.description: A backend service shall subscribe to MQTT topics, aggregate real-time slot data, and maintain an up-to-date parking occupancy map accessible via API.

functional_requirements.title: Driver-Facing Availability Interface
functional_requirements.description: Provide a simple interface (mobile web app or dashboard) showing real-time available slots with color-coded indicators (green=free, red=occupied) and optional navigation guidance.

functional_requirements.title: Sensor Node Configuration & OTA Updates
functional_requirements.description: Support remote configuration of sensor thresholds and MQTT topics, and enable over-the-air (OTA) firmware updates for ESP32 nodes via secure HTTPS.

functional_requirements.title: System Health Monitoring & Alerts
functional_requirements.description: Monitor node connectivity, sensor health, and message latency; generate alerts for offline nodes or anomalous readings (e.g., stuck occupied state > 24h).

non_functional_requirements.title: Low Hardware Cost per Slot
non_functional_requirements.description: Total bill of materials (BOM) per sensor node (ESP32, sensor, enclosure, power) shall not exceed $15 USD at 100-unit volume to ensure scalability.

non_functional_requirements.title: Battery Life for Wireless Nodes
non_functional_requirements.description: Battery-powered sensor nodes shall operate for ≥12 months on a single charge (e.g., 18650 Li-ion or 4x AA) using deep sleep and event-driven wakeups.

non_functional_requirements.title: Detection Accuracy & Latency
non_functional_requirements.description: Occupancy detection shall achieve ≥98% accuracy with ≤2 seconds latency from vehicle arrival/departure to MQTT status update under normal conditions.

non_functional_requirements.title: Network Resilience & Offline Buffering
non_functional_requirements.description: Sensor nodes shall buffer up to 50 status events locally during WiFi/MQTT outages and automatically reconnect and flush upon recovery.

non_functional_requirements.title: Scalability to 500+ Slots
non_functional_requirements.description: System architecture shall support ≥500 concurrent sensor nodes per MQTT broker instance with <100ms end-to-end latency at peak load.

non_functional_requirements.title: Environmental Robustness
non_functional_requirements.description: Outdoor sensor enclosures shall meet IP65 rating; operate reliably from -10°C to +50°C; resist vibration, dust, and condensation.

non_functional_requirements.title: Security & Access Control
non_functional_requirements.description: MQTT communication shall use TLS 1.2+ with client certificate authentication; backend API shall enforce role-based access (admin, viewer).

constraints: Total hardware cost per slot ≤ $15 (BOM at volume)
Project timeline: 2-3 months from idea to MVP deployment
Development team limited to 2-3 engineers (embedded + backend + frontend)
Must use ESP32 and MQTT as core technologies
No existing infrastructure assumed (power, networking, cloud) — must be self-contained or use low-cost cloud (e.g., MQTT on Raspberry Pi / free tier AWS IoT)
Regulatory: Unlicensed ISM band (2.4 GHz WiFi) compliance; no LoRaWAN/cellular due to cost
assumptions: Parking facility has WiFi coverage (2.4 GHz) across all slots or can deploy low-cost APs
Each slot can accommodate a small sensor node mounted on ceiling, wall, or ground
Power available for gateway/broker; sensor nodes may be battery or solar-assisted
Driver interface can be a progressive web app (PWA) — no native app store deployment needed
MQTT broker can be hosted on-premises (e.g., Raspberry Pi 4 + Mosquitto) or free cloud tier
Vehicle detection via ultrasonic (HC-SR04) or IR break-beam is sufficient; no license plate recognition required
open_questions: What is the exact parking layout (indoor/outdoor, multi-level, slot dimensions)? Affects sensor choice and mounting.
Is AC power available at each slot, or must all nodes be battery/solar powered?
What is the target deployment size for MVP (e.g., 10 slots, 50, 100)?
Who owns the WiFi infrastructure — can we deploy dedicated APs or must use existing guest network?
Are there local regulations on RF emissions, data privacy, or surveillance (cameras not used, but sensors may be regulated)?
What backend/cloud budget is available beyond 'low cost' — e.g., $0/month, $20/month?
Is integration with existing parking management or payment systems required?
